_comment: The video taxonomy of the kit (layer A, inbuilt). Read-only in an install. VIDEO-ANATOMY.md explains every slot; learnings-video.md gives the reasons. A local overlay (apps/<slug>/niche/video/patterns.json, written by the video-evidence step when it exists) references these ids and adds scoped evidence; it never redefines an id. Twelve hook jobs and eight recipes: adding one needs a structural reason and a new taxonomy_version.

phrasings.note: an asked-for premise; the request is sourced or plainly scripted
the counter is an overlay; the day is real

phrasings.phrase: Never do this / stop doing this
phrasings.note: a warning is a promise with negative framing
POV is a framing, not a filming format

phrasings.phrase: I do this for a living
phrasings.note: only a real, verified speaker or a sourced fact

phrasings.phrase: Reaction / a reacting face / “I just found this??”
phrasings.note: never spoken: a silent reacting face with the hook as text, performed from a real reference reaction (user decision, 2026-10-03)

runnable.definition: P1 to P6 make it today: T talking segments; T, O, G, S, H, F, R, P with app insertion

bridge.B.definition: generated action: silent hands, pet-only action or an approved mascot, exact subject counts

bridge.C.definition: supplied media: clips and stills beside R and P, trimmed, checksummed, subject-bound, source-approved at gate B

bridge.narration.definition: a narrator apart from the face: character audio over action, a supplied voice, an approved original synthetic narrator

bridge.composition.definition: split screen, picture in picture of two sources, timed overlay tracks, source credits, series counters

bridge.live.definition: a real input clip paired with the app recording that read it, with measured input and output times

bridge.reaction.definition: a silent generated face of an approved character, performed from a real reference reaction (expression beats, head, eyes, framing, distance), under a timed hook overlay; requested from production, not declared yet

patterns.definition: A familiar activity done for a long time, then a late discovery.
constraints: elapsed_time is true for the persona or the user's plan; never invented
aliases: seven years shopping at X, now I found this
and I'm JUST NOW finding this??

patterns.definition: A deadline close at hand and a job not yet done.
constraints: the deadline is the persona's situation, not a claim about the viewer
aliases: Vet appointment in 1 HOUR and I just found this

patterns.definition: A small admitted belief or habit, then its correction.
constraints: sounds true; no melodrama

patterns.definition: A doubter's line, then the answer.
constraints: the quote is a common saying or sourced; no invented second speaker or credential

patterns.definition: A task and the useful result the video delivers.
constraints: the result is delivered inside the video
aliases: This is how often you need to…

patterns.definition: A shared moment and a question a peer would ask.
A before and an after shown in the first beat.
constraints: the result is real footage or a real screen

patterns.definition: A task already underway; the action itself holds attention. No hook sentence is needed.
constraints: the channel may be visual only

patterns.definition: Thanks to a person who showed the creator something useful.
constraints: no extra character plays the person
no invented endorsement: the person showed it, they did not endorse it
the premise is true for the persona or plainly scripted
aliases: I could literally kiss the … who showed me this

patterns.definition: A familiar product category applied to a new subject.
constraints: the analogy names a shared job, never a capability the app does not have
aliases: Someone made a baby tracker but for cats??

patterns.definition: Something kept from an audience, then the payoff.
constraints: uses setup_reveal; the reveal is real
aliases: Do NOT show this to a cat mom

patterns.definition: An observed sign or a question, its meaning, and one action.
constraints: health and risk meanings cite a real source
no credential claimed by a fictional persona
aliases: This is the reason your cat…
This is what it means when…

patterns.definition: Sell one job with one mechanism and one answered doubt.
constraints: mechanism and doubt filled from facts
one doubt
paid may close with product_action

patterns.definition: Attention, then the real use, then its real result.
constraints: the app may be the last result
a separate discovery sentence and a closing payoff are optional

patterns.definition: A task underway, its actions, a log or check, and on.
constraints: app optional
zero spoken app names allowed
no CTA required
a meaningful task, not scenery

patterns.definition: An admission, a specific experience, what changed, a reflection.
constraints: product optional
invented testimonials forbidden

patterns.definition: State or approach A, an intervention or contrast, state B, a takeaway.
constraints: comparison_mode set
same subjects and context in A and B
no unsupported causal claim

patterns.definition: A sign or question, its explanation, one action.
constraints: app absent, or one incidental mid-video line or screen (app_aside)
risk and health facts cite real sources
no invented doubt, transformation or credential

patterns.definition: A specific promise, n items or steps, a takeaway.
constraints: items carry repeat_group and item_index
one app may take one numbered item

patterns.definition: A situation or tease, the revealed message or result, an optional response.
constraints: a notification, a forbidden reveal and a product punchline share this structure
the revealed message or result is real

patterns.definition: An approved handle rule bounds every slot; an exception needs the user's explicit, dated decision.
A visible app is the real app through app insertion (app_insertion true). No generated, drawn or overlaid UI; an overlay never carries the app's real words or a clinical result.
A numeric, health, risk or product claim names a fact reference or a real screen.
Hook slots are filled from the plan, product facts or a source; never an invented elapsed time, result, credential, request or quotation.
A real animal is shown only in supplied footage; never generated, never replaced by generated footage.
At most 15 spoken words per 4 seconds of a beat; overlays stay up at least words ÷ 3 seconds, and 1 second minimum.
No credential for a fictional persona or a synthetic voice; a synthetic narrator never speaks over a visible human face (a mascot can have a synthetic voice-over) and is never a clone.
One primary ask at most; a paid product_action close needs a real destination.
Delayed product and a payoff close are starter defaults for organic pitch only, below the handle's strategy; early demonstration is valid for discovery; 'name once' does not apply to everyday.
A reaction hook is never spoken: a silent reacting face (silent_action, face, no line, no voice-over) with the hook as a text overlay that starts in the first beat.

A reaction is never invented. video-plan picks a real reference reaction from the workspace's downloaded research (a post id and the exact time range); video-script writes the performance from it (expression beats, timing, head, eyes, framing, distance to the camera). No reference blocks the plan. The reference gives the performance only; the face is the handle's approved character, never the reference creator.

sources.note: Discovery regret → face → real demo/result; value legible in the store/budget/output sequence. One post holds 83.4% of attributed reach: an example's views are not a promised result.
Same face-to-demo format with an imminent-need or regret hook; a moving input-to-map mechanism. Its numbered feature explainers were weak.

sources.ref: research corpus: UMax TEARDOWN.md §§ 4, 6 and the sample caveats
sources.note: Serial action, visible state changes, caption placement; many creatives show no app UI. Only 428 of 1,691 sampled posts name UMax: untagged reach is niche evidence, not proven promotion.
Face-to-screen demonstration; the product as the useful result at about 2–6 s. Gym B-roll with caption-only promotion was weak: four accounts, 200 posts, 465,304 views.
Specific personal situations; caption suffix as placement. Much of the text-led evidence is photo mode, not video. Weak skits do not show that all skits lose.

X articles; authors sell tools or services; paid-ad bias. One idea, one mechanism, one doubt; facts match real screens; 15 words per 4 s. Early reveal, compulsory naming and the product-free close are scoped choices.
Slideshow hooks; transfer to video is not proven.
Reaction hooks are never spoken; reactions are never invented, they come from a real reference reaction in the user's own research. A mascot may have a synthetic voice-over.

sources.ref: a founder's handle strategies and experiment universe, coverage audit 2026-10-03
sources.note: Planned cells, never observed posts. Shows the jobs are needed; says nothing about whether they win.

examples.annotation: Face reacts with a regret line (attention), the real app is used (use_reveal), its output is read (result). Product at about 2–6 s.
examples.limitation: Timing differs from paid-ad defaults; one post dominates the reach.

examples.annotation: A serial action with visible state change and text; no app on screen.
examples.limitation: Reach without the app named is niche evidence, not proof of promotion.

examples.annotation: Counter-example: scenery with caption-only promotion. A routine needs a meaningful task.
examples.limitation: Four accounts; scoped to that niche.
